answer: In an attestation graph, bounded random walks spread trust only across reachable, well-supported paths, limiting the influence of isolated identities. A Sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance, so few walks cross its boundary; under capped per-node voting and bounded walk length, its aggregate voting weight is correspondingly constrained. Edge labels such as umber, velvet, and ferrous do not alter this bound unless the protocol assigns them weight.
